sources.title: Mem0 Raises $24M Series A to Build Memory Layer for AI Agents
sources.summary: Press release for Mem0's $24M Series A (Oct 28, 2025). Gives investor list, traction metrics and the AWS Agent SDK exclusivity that anchors the 'memory layer is a funded category' narrative.
key_facts: Mem0 raised $24M total: Series A led by Basis Set Ventures, seed led by Kindred Ventures (announced Oct 28, 2025)
Series A participants: Peak XV Partners, GitHub Fund, Y Combinator; angels Scott Belsky and Dharmesh Shah
Angel CEOs from Datadog, Supabase, PostHog, ex-GitHub and Weights & Biases also invested
Traction at announcement: 41,000 GitHub stars and 14M downloads
API calls grew from 35M in Q1 2025 to 186M in Q3 2025 (5.3x in two quarters)
AWS chose Mem0 as exclusive memory provider for its Agent SDK; CrewAI, Flowise, Langflow integrate natively

sources.title: Mem0 funding, news & analysis
sources.summary: Sacra company profile for Mem0: funding history, business model and competitor map. No revenue/ARR estimate disclosed.
key_facts: Mem0 total raised $24M across seed and Series A since founding in late 2023; CEO Taranjeet Singh, SF
Pricing is usage-based, billed on memory operations; deployments span cloud SaaS, private VPC, Kubernetes, air-gapped on-prem
Claimed economics: compressed memory snippets cut prompt token usage by up to 80% vs full conversation history
May 2025: AWS selected Mem0 as exclusive memory provider for Strands Agent SDK
Competitor map: vertically integrated labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta); Zep, Letta, LangMem, LlamaIndex Memory; vector DBs Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, Qdrant expanding into memory
No ARR, revenue or valuation figures disclosed

sources.title: The AI Memory Problem: How Mem0, Letta & Zep Give Agents Persistent Context
sources.summary: VC-authored comparison of the three funded memory startups, with a diligence framing on why a narrow infra layer every agent needs can compound into a moat.
key_facts: Letta raised a $10M seed in September 2024 led by Felicis Ventures (angels incl. Jeff Dean, Clem Delangue per search snippet)
Mem0 cited at $24.5M total funding; 186M API calls in Q3 2025; 41k-48k GitHub stars; 14M downloads
Zep funding amount not disclosed in the article
Thesis quote: 'a narrow, hard infrastructure layer that every agent needs compounds a real [moat]'
Claim: 65% of enterprise AI agent failures trace to context drift, not model capability (attribution not given)
Pricing tiers: Mem0 free-$249/mo; Zep from $25/mo credit-based; Letta self-hosted or usage-based
Earliest paying adopters: support and internal-tools teams, because churn cost is measurable

sources.title: 2025: The State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
sources.summary: Menlo's annual enterprise survey (N=495, Nov 2025) with a full spend stack-up. Key for this market: RAG is the #2 customization technique, context engineering is still 'niche', and only 16% of enterprise deployments are true agents.
key_facts: Enterprise GenAI spend $37B in 2025, up from $11.5B in 2024 (3.2x) and ~$1.7B in 2023
Applications $19B (51%): departmental $7.3B, horizontal $8.4B, vertical $3.5B
Infrastructure $18B (49%): foundation model APIs $12.5B, model training infra $4.0B, other AI infra $1.5B
Only 16% of enterprise deployments and 27% of startup deployments are 'true agents' that plan, act, observe, adapt
Customization: prompt design dominant; RAG second-most common; context engineering, tool calling, fine-tuning, RL 'niche and used primarily by frontier teams'
Survey: 495 U.S. enterprise AI decision-makers, Nov 7-25, 2025
Report contains no explicit figures on vector DB adoption or memory-layer spend

Only ~10% of that, about $750M, went to agentic AI platforms that act autonomously on users' behalf (as reported by No Jitter)

sources.title: How 100 Enterprise CIOs Are Building and Buying Gen AI in 2025
sources.summary: a16z's May 2025 CIO survey. Relevant signals: LLM budgets growing ~75%, multi-model use rising (which raises the value of provider-agnostic memory/context layers), and agentic workflows raising switching costs. Notably silent on RAG, vector DBs, memory and observability.
key_facts: 100 CIOs across 15 industries surveyed plus 24+ in-depth buyer interviews (published May 8, 2025)
LLM budgets expected to grow ~75% over next year; innovation-budget share fell from 25% to 7% as spend moved to permanent lines
37% of respondents use 5+ models in production, up from 29% prior year
CIO quote: 'what I spent in 2023 I now spend in a week'
Switching costs rising because agentic workflows require significant re-engineering to move between models
Fine-tuning seen as less necessary due to better models and longer context windows
CIOs prefer usage-based pricing over outcome-based; over 90% testing third-party customer-support apps
No mention of RAG, vector databases, memory systems or observability tools anywhere in the survey

sources.title: 6 data predictions for 2026: RAG is dead, what's old is new again and the future of vector databases
sources.summary: Year-end predictions piece arguing vectors are becoming a data type inside multimodel databases (narrowing pure-play vector DB use cases) while contextual memory becomes table stakes for agents. Also tallies 2025 data-infra M&A.
key_facts: Prediction: contextual/agentic memory becomes 'table stakes' for operational agentic AI deployments in 2026
Memory systems that emerged in 2025: Hindsight, A-MEM, GAM, LangMem, Memobase
Vectors shifted from specialized database type to a data type in Oracle, Google databases and Amazon S3; purpose-built vector DB use cases will narrow in 2026
2025 M&A: Snowflake bought Crunchy Data for $250M; Databricks bought Neon for $1B; IBM to acquire Confluent for $11B; Salesforce bought Informatica for $8B
Supabase raised $100M Series E at a $5B valuation; Meta invested $14.3B in Scale AI
PostgreSQL became the default choice for GenAI solutions in 2025; Snowflake launched agentic document analytics extending RAG across thousands of sources
Thesis: durable data infrastructure, not clever prompts, determines which deployments scale in 2026
